strategyPosture: Position for rotation, not rollover: hold index risk while lending standards are loose and HY OAS is 3.24, and concentrate any entry sizing on the DATA_AHEAD troughs (AVGO, BWXT, VST) with tier discipline — nothing new into the derated software names until the verify-first flags clear.

themes.counterRead: Index calm is compositional: SPY's level masks real damage concentrated in the handful of names that dominate it by weight. The credit data (loose lending, tight HY spreads) is what keeps this a rotation read rather than a rollover — but that is a conditional, not a conclusion. Credit flips fast, and the -9.11 pt divergence is the largest warning sign on the board.
themes.dataAnchor: Mag7 averages -10.31% from 52-week highs while SPY is only -1.2% — a -9.11 point divergence, with TSLA the weakest at -25.7% and NVDA strongest at -1.7%. Bank lending standards are LOOSE (SLOOS 0%, far below the ~40% stress threshold), HY OAS is 3.24, and the 2s10s curve is positively sloped at +0.50. QQQ is +5.68% on the month while IWM is -4.21% — money is moving, not leaving. Macro legs carry a staleness asterisk: the FRED feed is PARTIAL this run (fred.stlouisfed.org timeouts, last-good cache).
themes.label: Index Rotation, Not Rollover
themes.narrative: The index looks calm — SPY is +0.61% over the last month at $769.86, and VIX fell 6.6% on the day to 15.31. The tape says risk-on.
themes.watchFor: Divergence gap wider than -12 pts or SLOOS lending standards above 10% flips the read from rotation to rollover.

themes.counterRead: The equipment cohort is already rebounding from the multiple-derating; AVGO hasn't. That gap is where the asymmetry sits — but AVGO's +55% revenue is trailing data, and the decline classifier only sees trailing revenue. The recovery read needs forward confirmation, not faith in the score.
themes.dataAnchor: AVGO's decline explanation is mechanical: revenue growing +55% YoY with 67.8% gross margin and a 42.1% FCF margin ($26,914M), scored 81 in the top-conviction list (tier A, RSI 47.6). The semis-equipment cohort already shows the derating was multiple compression, not demand collapse: AMAT is -27% from highs but +23.2% this month (RSI 69.2), LRCX -20.8% but +20.5% this month, ONTO -15.2% but +28.8% this month, KLAC -32.7% but +20.1% this month. The watchlist labels AVGO's revenue inflection RECOVERY.
themes.label: AI Infrastructure: Price Derated, Fundamentals Not
themes.narrative: The AI-infra trade is over — AVGO sits -28.3% below its high and semis equipment names are 15-33% off their peaks.
themes.watchFor: AVGO RSI14 above 55 and a close within 20% of its 52-week high upgrades entry quality.

themes.counterRead: The policy bid is landing on operators (VST) and equipment (BWXT), not on fuel — buy the two screened names, not the theme. VST's internally conflicting revenue signals (DETERIORATING inflection in the watchlist vs +19.1% trailing growth in the conviction list) mean a thesis check before any sizing, not blind averaging into the -35.5% drawdown.
themes.dataAnchor: VST, a holding, is -35.5% from its 52-week high at $140.02 with insiders buying $1.17M at the trough; it scores 76 (tier B) at 2.7x P/S. BWXT is -44.2% at $134.86 with revenue growing +18.3% YoY (score 77, RSI 30.4). But uranium/fuel names are not participating: CCJ is -11.09% on the month and SMR -18.51% sit in the laggards list. The watchlist itself flags VST's revenue inflection as DETERIORATING even while the top-conviction screen prints +19.1% revenue growth.
themes.label: Nuclear: Policy Heat Against a Deep Drawdown
themes.narrative: Nuclear is the power story of the cycle — the high-signal headline this morning is the Trump administration reportedly preparing a $4B federal loan to expand Vistra's nuclear capacity.
themes.watchFor: Confirmation of the reported $4B Vistra loan (headline plus filing) or VST closing to within -25% of its 52-week high with RSI above 55.

themes.counterRead: The pipeline's SENTIMENT_DRIVEN labels are auto-generated from trailing revenue + price decline and cannot see guidance trajectory — and this morning's own data proves the blind spot: TMDX, down -48.8%, carries the highest-materiality headline (a Q1 earnings and revenue miss with falling margins) — a genuine fundamental break wearing a sentiment label.
